data.narrative:
Verne is a Seed-stage climate and energy company that has raised $17.5M to date. The relevant comp universe spans 9 private peers (including Helion, Redwood Materials, and Electric Hydrogen) and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though none of these peers operate at sufficient similarity in stage or valuation tier to support a reliable peer-median benchmark.

Given the limited narrow comp set, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($18M) as a proxy for post-money value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $44M. This method is the primary quantitative anchor available given comp scarcity in the Climate & Energy sector at this stage and scale.

The triangulated valuation range is $37M to $50M, with a median of $44M. This narrow band reflects dependence on a single applicable method rather than true triangulation. Key uncertainties include: whether the 2.5x step-up multiplier appropriately captures Verne's specific risk and unit economics relative to later-stage peers, and whether the broader Climate & Energy comp set (absent tighter filters) would materially shift the implied range if sufficient near-peer data became available. Further diligence on revenue traction, capital efficiency, and technology differentiation relative to named peers would be required to validate or adjust this range.
